AbstractText.Label: Motivation
AbstractText.content: Differential network analysis is an important way to understand network rewiring involved in disease progression and development. Building differential networks from multiple `omics data provides insight into the holistic differences of the interactive system under different patient-specific groups. DINGO was developed to infer group-specific dependencies and build differential networks. However, DINGO and other existing tools are limited to analyze data arising from a single platform, and modeling each of the multiple 'omics data independently does not account for the hierarchical structure of the data.

AbstractText.Label: Results
AbstractText.content: We developed the iDINGO R package to estimate group-specific dependencies and make inferences on the integrative differential networks, considering the biological hierarchy among the platforms. A Shiny application has also been developed to facilitate easier analysis and visualization of results, including integrative differential networks and hub gene identification across platforms.

AbstractText.Label: Availability
AbstractText.content: R package available on CRAN (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/iDINGO), Shiny application at https://github.com/MinJinHa/iDINGO.

AbstractText.Label: Supplementary information
AbstractText.content: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.
